_about: Story scenes (closes: true shuts the talk window at the scene's end): a conversation that plays when Sera talks to someone, once, when what it waits on has happened. speaker: the unique character (uniques.json id) who starts it. when: {after: [chronicle events, all needed], unless: [events], days (that long since the last of them)}. lines: [who, what they say], who a unique id or "sera". records: chronicle events written when it's done. joins: a unique who joins Sera's party as it ends.

scenes.speaker: elder
lines: Miyu? Miyu! Is she... Sera, is she...?
She's breathing. I found her on the road up north. She'd got out of that village and fallen on her way home. She hasn't woken, but she isn't hurt badly.
Oh, thank the stars. Her colour's coming back already, look.
Bring her inside, quickly. Put her in the bed in our house, where it's warm.

scenes.speaker: elder
lines: Sera. You brought her back. You brought my Miyu back.
She's sleeping now. Not a scratch on her that won't heal. I don't know how we'll ever repay you.
You don't have to. I'm glad I got there in time. The village she was in... there was nobody else.
Then it's as we feared. Whatever is coming, it isn't stopping at our fence.
I'm an old man, Sera. I can keep the peace at the table, but I can't keep this village alive through what's coming. You can. You've already shown it.
Take the village into your keeping. The people will follow you: I've seen how they look at you, ears and all.
...All right. I'll look after them. All of them.
And Miyu, when she wakes. She'll want to go with you, you know. She's been watching you since the moment you came.
Hey! You there! Please... you have to help us!
Our village is being attacked by monsters. Please help! You look like an adventurer.
The mist suddenly came, and the beasts started acting strange!
They never come at us like this. They're not acting right. Please, we can't hold them!

scenes.speaker: elder
lines: It's quiet. Is it... is it over?
What was that? The mist, the monsters, all of it. Where did it come from?
And those things that looked like people. They were people, weren't they.
I can't believe it's already spread this fast. The mist was already happening everywhere else; I came to help spread the news of how to defend against it.
We can make makeshift pillars using these crystals. You're safe from the mist when you're around one.
Thank you for saving us. It's nice that you were just around.
I was resting near the river when your friend alerted me.
We've lost good people tonight. But we're still here. For now, help us repair the village.

scenes.speaker: elder
lines: Is that... you cooked for all of us? Thank you, Sera.
I'll share it out. Everyone needs something warm in them tonight.

scenes.speaker: elder
lines: You knew just what to do with that crystal. As if you'd done it before.
I have. The mist is already in other places, further off. I go where it goes, and help where I can.
A wanderer, then. And a peculiar one, if you'll forgive an old man for saying it.
It's not often we see one of your kind, with ears like those, helping folk like us. Not with how your people are treated.
I suppose I'm a little unique that way.
Unique or not, you've a bed here tonight. And a meal, though you cooked it yourself.
Now go and rest, Sera. You've done more than enough for one night.

scenes.speaker: miyu
lines: ...Sera? It's you. Grandfather says you carried me all the way home.
You were lying on the road north. You'd got yourself out of that village alone, you know. That took some doing.
I don't remember much of it. The mist came down, and everyone was shouting, and then... just the road. I kept walking.
Thank you. Truly. If you hadn't come, I'd still be out there. Or worse.
Rest a while longer. You're safe now.
I've rested enough for a lifetime. Let me come with you. I know these roads, and I can look after myself.
...All right. Stay close, and no more errands on your own.

scenes.speaker: miyu
lines: Sera... can I ask you something? How does it feel, when you call fire like that? Or your shikigami?
Warm, mostly. Like holding your breath, then letting it all go at once.
I'd give anything to feel that. Just once. I've watched you every time, you know. I even try the gestures when nobody's looking.

That's why I went to the next village, really. Grandfather thinks it was for thread. There's an old woman there with a shelf of books, and one of them is a book of magic. She'd promised to lend it to me.
I'd only just got there when the mist came down. Then the shouting... I never even saw the book.
It might! Whatever's left in that village is just lying there now. If you went back, and found it, and gave it to me...
...I don't know what would happen. Something, maybe. Something good.
